facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with an enlarging purpuric patch on his left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
initially present for 2 weeks
the lesion first developed in March 2014 and was fairly stable until June 2014
rapid growth and extension followed by central ulceration and bleeding
a 30 × 25-cm centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
involving: Left anterior scalp with extension posteriorly on left parietal scalp
No evidence of lymphadenopathy in preauricular, cervical, occipital, submandibular or supraclavicular areas
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5
No evidence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases
Staging: T2N0M0

concepts.why: The presence of rapid growth, ulceration, and bleeding, along with the histopathological findings of irregular slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and cells staining positively with CD31, are consistent with angiosarcoma.

The clinical presentation of a purpuric patch with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with the histopathological findings, could be consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma.

The presence of a purpuric patch with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with the histopathological findings of irregular slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes, could be consistent with hemangioma.
The clinical presentation of a rapidly growing lesion with ulceration and bleeding, along with the absence of lymphadenopathy, could be consistent with lymphoma.

The clinical presentation of a purpuric patch with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with the histopathological findings, could be consistent with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.
